Subject: Post-demo procurement intake & payment constraints — KiteBridge evaluation

Hi Sienna / Tom —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a few open items so we can map the commercial path:

- Procurement preference: you mentioned AP prefers PO for SOWs >$50k, and card for ad-hoc purchases under that threshold. Can you confirm the threshold and whether two-step approval is required for POs?
- Marketplace: you asked if Redwood is listed on the cloud marketplace (you mentioned procurement wants vendor/marketplace onboarding). Short answer: yes, we have a marketplace listing but there are vendor enrollment steps and an onboarding form. If procurement prefers marketplace billing vs vendor PO, that can simplify the payment route.
- Billing contacts: can you introduce the procurement contact (name + email) so we can share our procurement checklist and SOW templates?
- Timing: you said decision by end of Q1 is realistic; what internal timeline does procurement operate on for PO issuance?

Next steps I propose:
1) Sienna/Tom — confirm procurement contact and PO threshold by end of this week.
2) Marissa — I’ll hand off procurement checklist + SOW draft to share once we have the contact.
3) Aditya — prep a short note on marketplace onboarding steps and expected timeline for enrollment.

I attached a short note capturing today’s procurement questions (KiteBridge_Procurement_Notes.pdf). I’ll follow up with the full checklist.

Thanks — Logan

Subject: Re: Post-demo procurement intake & payment constraints — KiteBridge evaluation

Thanks Logan — useful recap. A few clarifications from procurement side:

- PO threshold: our finance policy requires an approved PO for any vendor engagement where committed spend exceeds $50,000 USD annually. For pilots and POCs expected under $50k, procurement typically allows payment via corporate card after vendor risk sign-off.
- Approvals: Senior procurement + legal sign-off for POs >$100k; below that it's a single-level AP approval but still requires a signed SOW.
- Marketplace: procurement prefers marketplace billing when available because it aligns with our procurement reporting, but vendor onboarding can take 3–4 weeks depending on vendor docs.

I’ve attached the internal vendor intake checklist we use (I redacted some internal codes). I’ll introduce our procurement lead, Erin Caldwell, separately — Erin will own the vendor paperwork.

We’re happy to review the SOW draft you mentioned; Tom and I will coordinate with Erin on timing.

Best — Sienna

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood procurement checklist + suggested MA plan

Hi Sienna / Tom —

Thanks for the quick notes, Sienna. Looping in a single-thread view of what we typically need to accelerate PO vs card decisions and to make marketplace enrollment smoother:

1) Vendor paperwork we can provide immediately:
   - W9 / vendor tax form
   - Standard Master Agreement + SOW template (we can pre-fill scope for pilot)
   - SOC 2 report + summary of data handling and retention policies

2) Typical procurement gating items (hit the common blockers):
   - PO approval cutoff: if pilot is expected to exceed $50k ask — we recommend structuring as two phases (pilot < $50k on card; expansion via PO) to speed initial work.
   - Marketplace vs vendor invoice: marketplace slightly faster for internal reporting but requires vendor enrollment; vendor invoice + PO is more flexible for custom SOWs.

3) Suggested mutual action plan (MA):
   - This week: procurement intro (Erin) + we share pre-filled SOW and onboarding checklist.
   - Week of Dec 6: 30-min vendor intake call with procurement to confirm docs and timeline.
   - Dec 13–17: Procurement issues PO or confirms corporate card route for pilot.

I attached our Redwood_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (clean version) and a pre-filled one-page pilot SOW to speed review. Aditya — can you outline the marketplace enrollment steps inline so Sienna’s team can evaluate tradeoffs?

Sienna — if Erin is comfortable we can route a short DocuSign for the SOW and then invoice via card or wait for PO depending on the path.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
